title: SB478 (2021-2022 Regular Session): Firearms; use or possession of any handgun in a park, historic site, or recreational area; provisions

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk dataset (gun-policy Stage 5 LegiScan check); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official legis.ga.gov PDF of the version named in note (via LegiScan getBillText)

operative_text:
SECTION 2 (amending O.C.G.A. 12-3-10(o)): (2) It shall be unlawful for any person to use or possess in any park, historic site, or recreational area any firearms other than a handgun, as such term is defined in Code Section 16-11-125.1. (3) It shall be unlawful for any person to use or possess in any park, historic site, or recreational area any handgun without a valid weapons carry license issued pursuant to Code Section 16-11-129.
SECTION 5 (amending O.C.G.A. 16-11-126): (a) Except as otherwise provided in subsection (b) of this Code section and Code Sections 16-11-127 through 16-11-127.2, 16-11-130.2, and 16-11-135, any Any person who is not prohibited by law from possessing a handgun or long gun may have: (1) Have or carry on his or her person a weapon or long gun on his or her property or inside his or her home, motor vehicle, or place of business without a valid weapons carry license.; or (b) Any person who is not prohibited by law from possessing a handgun or long gun may have or carry on his or her person a long gun without a valid weapons carry license, provided that if the long gun is loaded, it shall only be carried in an open and fully exposed manner.
SECTION 5 (amending O.C.G.A. 16-11-126): (c) Any person who is not prohibited by law from possessing a handgun or long gun may have or carry any handgun provided that it is enclosed in a case and unloaded.
SECTION 5 (amending O.C.G.A. 16-11-126): (g)(c) Notwithstanding Code Sections 12-3-10, 27-3-1.1, 27-3-6, and 16-12-122 through 16-12-127, any person with a valid weapons carry license may carry a weapon in all parks, historic sites, or recreational areas, as such term is defined in Code Section 12-3-10, including all publicly owned buildings located in such parks, historic sites, and recreational areas, in wildlife management areas, and on public transportation; provided, however, that a person shall not carry a handgun into a place where it is prohibited by federal law.
SECTION 6 (amending O.C.G.A. 16-11-127): (b) Except as provided in Code Section 16-11-127.1 and subsection (d) or (e) of this Code section, a person shall be guilty of carrying a weapon or long gun in an unauthorized location and punished as for a misdemeanor when he or she carries a weapon or long gun while: (1) In a government building as a nonlicense holder; (2)(1) In a courthouse; (3)(2) In a jail or prison;
SECTION 7 (amending O.C.G.A. 16-11-127.1(b)): (2) Except as provided for in paragraph (20) of subsection (c) of this Code section, any license holder person otherwise authorized under law to possess a weapon who violates this subsection shall be guilty of a misdemeanor. Any person who is not a license holder not otherwise authorized under law to possess a weapon who violates this subsection shall be guilty of a felony and, upon conviction thereof, be punished by a fine of not more than $10,000.00, by imprisonment for not less than two nor more than ten years, or both.
SECTION 11 (amending O.C.G.A. 16-11-137(b)): (b) A person carrying a weapon shall not be subject to detention for the sole purpose of investigating whether such person has a weapons carry license.
SECTION 20 (repealing O.C.G.A. 43-38-10): Said title is further amended by repealing Code Section 43-38-10, relating to permits to carry firearms by private detective businesses, proficiency requirement, exemption from specified laws, denial, refusal to renew, and suspension of permits, and effect of license suspension and restoration, and designating such Code section as reserved.
